The Great Free State Chicken Fiasco

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What is happening at Free State department of Rural Development of land reform, and why are so many of its projects wildly expensive failures? Carte Blanche exposes how two chicken farms and almost R1

Unique Selling Point:
We have photo's and documentation from the original deal as well as photo's from a year and a half ago where the farm has been stripped
We also have Ollie Le Roux who built the farm up from nothing for an on camera interview
We also have confirmation that even though the farm will need R22 million to get it back up to speed the beneficiary is planning another project on the farm - a poultry abattoir

Summary:
. We go in search of those responsible and find that even as the president promises to clamp down on corruption, out of the public eye, on the plains of the Free State, the politically connected are still going about their business.

WildealsKloof or Two Geese, one rugby player and no chickens
Eight years ago rugby player Ollie Le Roux sold his prime farm just outside Bloemfontein for R35 million rand to the Free State Department of Agriculture and Rural development. It was fully operational with 500 000 chickens, 300 pigs, 45 sheep and two cattle. There were 16 broiler houses, a cattle feedlot, 38 pigsties, 201 hectares of grazing ( CB has the official documents and photo’s taken of the audit at the time- even down to the desk and chairs.)

The total registered value at the time was R38 million rand (land and immovable assets) and the lucky beneficiary was Gertrude Bohloko’s company Two Geese Trading. According to Ollie Le Roux the farm would have given Ms Bohloka a very comfortable income and enable her to easily pay of the R150 000 rand monthly lease fee to the department. But by 2016 Bohloka had run the farm into the ground and pleaded poverty. She took Liberty to court to try to access her pension fund but lost the case, and her 5 bedroom, 3 bathroom home in Fichardt Park was auctioned off by ABSA.



Further information:
WHO IS GERTRUDE BOHLOKA?
Three independent sources have told Carte Blanche she is extremely powerful, connected to Ace Magashule and casts fear into the hearts of lesser mortals. The man who arranged the farm for her in the department – Steven Modise would drop everything to attend to her when she phoned.

THE FATE OF WILDEALSKLOOF
Now in 2020 the farm is in dire need of love and care – items have been stolen and the once busy farm is a shadow of its former self and the only activity says Ollie Le Roux is Gertrude on her mower mowing the lawn, which is unusual he says. Le Roux has a second farm across the road and has watched his former farm which he built from scratch disintegrate. Sometimes he helps his former workers with food when Bohloka just doesn’t pay them.

By 2017 the 5 year lease expired and despite the fact that Bohloka had not fulfilled the written provisions of the lease which is in Carte Blanche’s possession, her lease was renewed – apparently for another 30 years (confirmation required on duration)

ENTER CHICKEN MAN CHARLES VAUQUELIN
Charles Vauquelin is a straight shooting, turnaround chicken man. He can take any failed chicken venture and turn it into a profit and what he saw on Wildealskloof broke his heart. So he approached Gertrude B and every other influential person he could think of in Bloemfontein including the ANC, a business man and various others, to sub lease the farm from Bohloka for R150 000 per month, and use the existing infrastructure to farm chickens. He had a market, and all the plans in place. He also met with MEC William Bulwane and Gertrude Bohloka to try and broker a deal. But Gertrude refused to budge and by February this year Charles went to Rainbow in KZN to work there. He will go on camera and can fly us over the farm should we wish. Charles and Ollie Le Roux are not mates. But what is interesting about both their experiences is that they both tried separately to reinvigorate the farm and both hit a stumbling block that independently of each other, they believe is political. So eight years later the farm remains idle and the infrastructure either collapsing or stolen.

BUT WAIT THERE IS MORE
While Wildealskloof is a lovely farm by all accounts, it has a shortage of one critical thing, water. Carte Blanche has been told by a reliable source that in and around 2012, at least 5 boreholes were drilled and no water was found. Over the years an arrangement was made with the neighbouring farm to pipe additional water into the farm but it seems Bohloka has fallen out with the neighbour.

ANOTHER DAY, ANOTHER PLAN
So it would seem odd then to introduce the idea of building a chicken abattoir on the farm with insufficient water. Because if there is one thing an abattoir needs its water. But Two Geese trading – Bohloka’s company is pushing ahead and the EIA for the abattoir is already underway and has been confirmed by Carte Blanche in writing and with the man doing the EIA – Danie Krynauw.

SO WHAT IS THE PROBLEM?
The water is one thing: “where will all the blood and the feathers go? “asks Charles. It’s a crazy idea. There is also no need for another abattoir in the region, there are already too many, says our secret source, and when he heard about the idea his immediate response was this is yet another attempt to siphon off millions from the state. Try R80 million rand at least.

And if Gertrude goes to a private bank for the money, it’s unlikely she will get a loan based on her not too stellar history in the chicken business; the fact that she doesn’t own the farm; and that there is no water on it. Which likely leaves only one avenue for Gertrude B – the Department of Rural Development and Land reform that has been so generous previously.

ENTER THE MEC WILLIAM BULWANE
So Carte Blanche phoned the MEC of Agriculture and Rural Dev and asked him if he knew about the project and how it will be financed. (recorded conversation) No he said, but he would find out. He said he didn’t know Gertrude Bohloka (not true, he does, and we can prove that ) but he was very nice and promised to get back to us, so we didn’t push the fact he has already been caught out lying by CB. According to Mxolisi Dukwana our timing is good because Ace’s people are trying to distance themselves from him – “so he might help you’ says Dukwana.

Just to put this money into perspective – Sun Valley farm managed to break even, pay salaries and all debt in 9 months with around R5 million and some borrowed tractors.
All they wanted from their department was a R12 million rand loan and it never came.

NOW LETS GO TO MEGA POULTRY IN VIRGINIA
Here in the Matjhabeng municipality you will find the Virginia Mega poultry project.

In 2014, two years after Gertrude began her farming venture, R30 million rand was spent on five broiler houses meant to house 40 000 chickens and meant to transform the lives of rural women. A year later another R9 million was spent and again R13 million in 2017 when the project was supposed to be complete. ( In China they build a hospital in ten days but anyway…) From the air this is what it looks like – and we have these pictures because poor old enthusiastic chicken man Charles Vauquelin hoped to get that business up and rolling too and flew over the area. But he didn’t succeed despite his proposals, and today the farms stand idle. (SEE BELOW) We also have a number of picture of Wildealskloof taken in 2012 when the farm was in good condition.

Gertrude Bholoka will likely send Carte Blanche on a wild goose chase but now that we have spoken to the MEC it is going to be difficult for him to duck and dive. Still trying to find out a bit more on who built the Virginia Mega Project but I don’t think that will be too difficult.

Both Charles V and Ollie Le Roux will go on camera. We can drone over the farms if access is denied but Ollie says he can get us on to Wilde Els Kloof.

Script:


THE GREAT FREE STATE CHICKEN FIASCO FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 4th OCTOBER 2020

Commentary One
You may remember Ollie Le Roux as a provincial and Springbok front row forward, making his mark in the toughest position in a very tough sport.

Up sound Ollie scores try

Derek Link
What you may not know is that he also made his mark in the demanding arena of poultry farming right here in the Free State

Commentary Two
Ollie met us on his farm just north of Bloemfontein

Up sound Ollie and Derek

Commentary Three
But it’s not rugby, but his first farm Wildealskloof that I am here to talk about, because Le Roux has first- hand experience of how a land reform project can go horribly wrong.

Music up sound

By 2012 he had built the farm into a profitable business with 16 broiler houses and a contract with Supreme to take 500 000 chickens every week

Ollie
It was a strong contract and if you farmed well you made money

Derek Link
in 2012 Le Roux sold his farm to the state. The farm was then leased to a beneficiary -Getrude Bohloko for five years. The chickens were already bringing in a healthy revenue,
all she had to do, was keep it going and reap the benefits

Derek
The bottom line is a beneficiary could make good money out of the farm?
Ollie
Very good.

Commentary Four
This valuation around the time of the sale, shows the state valued the farm at almost R42 million rand, with the assets ranging from average to good condition.

Derek
Just to refresh your memory I am going to ask our producer to show you these pictures of the farm at that stage


Ollie
That old chair you guys are going to get me all emotional now..

Commentary Five
These photos were part of an official asset verification done in 2013 -and listed almost every item Le Roux had left for the new owner.

Ollie
The infrastructure you know it looks easy but jis, it takes a lot of stress and strain, but it’s a privilege to be able to create something like this
Derek
How did you feel about selling the farm Ollie?
Ollie
To leave it, and leave the people that you …it’s like leaving rugby. There is a lot of emotion in the land so I understand why land is such a powerful thing for people.

Commentary Six
The price agreed upon was R39.5 million voetstoets, and by 2013 Getrude Bohloko’s company was running the farm.

Chickens up sound

But just two years later Supreme cancelled the valuable contract. It seems Bohloko didn’t honour her side of the agreement and began costing them money. Then her company tried to go it alone

Ollie
They never understood how precious the contract is, and everybody thinks we can do it on our own, but trust me Derek you don’t understand 500 000 chickens with blood and feathers, you need big infrastructure and if the market goes against you, you are sitting with 500 000 frozen product. It’s a very tough game

Derek Link
Fast forward to 2017, and these pictures in our possession tell a sad story, of a farm stripped and broken, the 500 000 chickens gone, the broiler houses closed up, and a few dirty pigs lying in muck.

Commentary seven
Workers weren’t paid and apparently some may have vandalised the farm, but Bohloko refused to participate in our story, to give her side of events

Derek
Ollie we are going to show you pictures of the farm in recent years, I don’t want to upset you but this is what it looks like


Ollie
Ay ay ya the old fiat in sy moer…Oh donder! Yoh that was a massive infrastructure you know with this we could work 500 animals a day with three people. Yoh the generators are gone and that is a lot of money gone. And it’s being vandalized…
Derek
So to recap that farm now Ollie
Ollie
You can do it but it’s going to cost what it cost to buy it
Derek
So who has lost out really?
Ollie
Everybody has lost.
Derek
The state has lost
Ollie
And 38 people you can just imagine that’s 120 families and there was such a hope this would be a flagship project. Just to look at it is just so sad

Commentary eight
How Land reform beneficiaries are chosen has been described as an opaque process, and more than one recent official report has red flagged how elites are muscling in to get farms. Sources alleged, Getrude Bohloko was one of those elites.

Up sound

Steven Modise an official in the Free State Land reform office, was part of the process that helped Bohloko get Wilde Alskloof.

Derek
What criteria were used to select Getrude Bohloko as a beneficiary?
Steven Actually she presented the offer of this farm to the department. Once you've identified your interest and your needs, you automatically become matched with a particular farm. And then once she was matched with a farm, obviously we acquired the farm as a department and then she then enjoys a lease

Commentary nine
At the time Modise was a director at Free State Land reform and recommended the funds be released for Wildealskloof. Our sources say it was Modise who wangled farms for elite beneficiaries

Derek
Steven we have independent sources telling us that you decide which politically connected people get the farms that are worth over R20 million?
Steven
Well it’s the first time I am hearing that I have never done anything for anybody, and for your information I am seated here today because I am the acting chief director acting for the last 3- 4 months – I am not involved in the allocation of farms, I am not involved…
Derek
Apparently you have been the go between
Steven
Well I didn’t know I was

Commentary ten
Bohloko’s lease expired in 2017 and her agreement with the state was to look after the assets or risk having the lease cancelled, that didn’t happen -instead it was decided last year to extend her lease for 30 years. Modise also told me the department visited the farm every quarter

Derek
But why didn't you step in when it was clear that the farm was failing and in fact being stripped
Steven
The farm was not failing, it was not stripped. In fact the stripping of the farm, If I were to tell you as far as I can recall when we bought the farm around 2012 was by the previous owner Mr. Leroux, who actually stripped the farm… so it was never stripped by any of our beneficiaries.

Commentary eleven
Le Roux says that’s a blatant lie and certainly the state’s own valuation and audit documents contradict Modise. The assets were considered in fair to good condition at the time of the sale.

Derek But if you've been visiting on a quarterly basis have you not seen what's happening there?
Just have a look at these pictures and you tell me that's not a farm going to wrack and ruin.
Steven
No, we know what is happening on the farm. These are the assets that were bought from Mr. Ollie Le Roux - They were bought in that state in a worse state
Derek
So you're saying those are the assets that she inherited in 2012?
Steven
No she didn't inherit the assets like this. But I want to come to that to actually explain to you.
Derek
Just to say that we've got pictures of when they were handed over.
Steven
Well you are saying they have been stripped? By whom? I don't know.




LINK
Two years after Wildealskloof was handed over, another chicken project about 150 kilometres north was under construction. The Virginia Mega poultry project- five broiler houses each with a capacity of 40 000 chickens

Commentary twelve
This poultry project, was built by E’tsho Civils, who said it would be complete by 2016. But six years since construction began and more than R52 million rand later, the project is at a standstill. E’tsho civils only director, is alleged in Pieter Louis Myburgh book, Gangster State to be close to ANC SG, Ace Magashule, who threatened to sue the author and hasn’t yet.

Dr Roy Jankielson
So it’s a huge financial basket with no eggs.

Commentary thirteen
THE DA’S Roy Jankielsohn has a PHD in Land reform modelling and has been on the Free state portfolio committee for Agriculture for 14 years.

Roy
In the Free State, agricultural projects are set up for the sole purpose of benefitting implementing agents and their cronies in government. I don’t think projects are set up in the FS to contribute to food security or assist beneficiaries on the ground
Derek
That is a strong statement Roy
Roy
It is a strong statement and I would stand by it because we have the necessary proof in the Free State

Commentary fourteen
Recently he has visited a number of farming projects and was shocked at the state of their decay. Here at Diyatalawa agricultural village, which cost R150 million rand – the dairy has been plundered, the apple trees are sticks, and just this gatehouse and fence alone, cost R600 000.

Roy
And I would challenge the MEC or any government official to prove otherwise- go and find us a project that is sustainable

Commentary Fifteen
MEC William Bulwane of the Department of Agriculture in the Free State disputes that, and has invited Carte Blanche to view their successful projects, which we will hopefully take up with them in the near future

Derek
I'm saying to you MEC see that the allegations are clear these projects are there to benefit the contractors who built the infrastructure, and the officials who hand out the contracts not the beneficiaries. In other words. Billions are being squandered- there is fraud, there is corruption, there is mismanagement?

MEC Bulwane
I like your word when you said allegations. It's a big word. Anybody squandering government money you know what must happen. And you can't just be sitting here folding our arms and be happy that government billions have been squandered
Derek
But you know they have?
MEC
Where? where?
Derek
What about the Estina Project?
MEC
Maybe you know where money has been squandered. I don't know? You must tell me so that when I leave from this seat I go there and take action.
Derek
Okay I'll give you two examples, you've got Wildealskloof you've got Virginia within about 150 kilometres of each other -and that's cost nearly a hundred million rand with nothing to show for it?
MEC
Now that you are talking figures I want the HOD to answer that question and then this billions you're talking about. I don't know where do you get them?

Commentary sixteen
Over the last five years R1.2 billion has been spent on farmer support in the Free State. It appears no one has done monitoring and evaluation to see if the funds were wisely spent to ensure beneficiaries become successful farmers, and even the auditor General can’t get an accurate picture because there are inadequate systems to record vital information.

Derek
MEC are you denying that a lot of money has been squandered?
MEC
No no, no…
Derek
In corruption and mismanagement in the Free STATE
MEC
We are not answering questions about corruption here, and I am saying this project we can account for, and I won’t agree with you that there is corruption
Derek
You will not agree that there has been any corruption in the Free State?
MEC
You have seen it yourself?
Derek
I have done programmes on it. What would you call Estina? The Virginia project, what would you call any of the projects that have lost millions, and have nothing to show for it

MEC
From where I am sitting, there is no money that has been squandered in Virginia, there is no money that has been squandered in that poultry project here
Derek
MEC you say there has been no squandering of money but neither project is operational?!
MEC
The Virginia project was operational, the water was getting inside those houses so they had to stop and build a storm water drainage

Commentary seventeen
So a new contractor was called in to fix the problematic storm water. The MEC had summonsed Dr Masiteng to answer specifics about Virginia, but most had already been answered by the MEC. Masiteng defended the R52 million price tag but did concede that the department needed to strengthen accountability

Derek
What is the plan for Virginia now?
MEC
They just need a strategic partner, once they have a strategic partner to share the expenses, and then they can move with speed.

Commentary eighteen
While it appears that nothing is moving with speed at Wildealskloof – behind the scenes there are new plans for the farm even though in eight years Bohloko only paid her
R150 000 annual lease, once.

Derek Link
It may seem odd that having failed at farming, Getrude Bohloko now wants to build an abattoir on her farm

Commentary nineteen
And the speculation is that it’s unlikely the private sector would fund Bohloko’s abattoir

Derek
Some people say that the poultry abattoir is just a way to siphon off money?
Ollie
I believe they are 100% correct. Where are you going to find money for a poultry abattoir you will go to the IDC or the DTI and you are going to go to the bank. Trust me the banks aren’t going to look at you. The IDC they are too sharp so they not going to fund a project like that I know them too well. But where are you going to get it you are going to look for a grant and just siphon of money and it’s going to cost the taxpayer money. Rather start the farm again let’s do it with banks money but to take our tax money build an abattoir that is guaranteed to fail, I believe that is where we as SA must say enough is enough now

Commentary twenty
Bohloko was clear she didn’t want to speak to us, but I gave it another shot anyway

Derek
And you still propose going ahead with the poultry abattoir?
Gertrude
I have confirmed in writing with Miss Summers and the poultry abattoir and the EIA is handled by the department of environmental affairs …please refer to the feedback I have given to miss Summers

Steven Modise
If she is bringing investment into that asset, that is the kind of beneficiary we want
Derek
But who is going to pay for that abattoir?
Steven Modise
She is sourcing her own funds
Derek
She is not asking for state funding?
Steven Modise
No, no
Derek
Putting it simply shouldn’t another beneficiary be given a chance to run that farm?
Steven Modise
We are not convinced that she has failed so much, that that farm cannot operate. That farm needs production capital, that farm needs a contract, so obviously once those things are in place that farm will get back into operation

Commentary twenty- one
But Bohloko had all that back in 2013, a debt free, operational farm worth R40 million. A management team left by Le Roux to help her, plus a government mentorship programme and a ten year offtake agreement for the chickens. It may only be one example, but we are told there are many others, and if this is how the Free State is managing their land reform projects, perhaps it’s time for a radical rethink.

THE END 16 05

PROMO ONE
Two Free State Poultry projects – cost to taxpayer close to R100 million. Both are at a standstill. We go to the top to find out what went wrong.

PROMO TWO
Former Springbok Rugby player Ollie Le Roux speaks out about the profitable poultry farm he sold to the state that now lies in wrack and ruin.

PROMO THREE
The Virginia Mega poultry project was meant to uplift local women. But six years and R52 million rand later and the project is still not operational.

Which likely leaves only one avenue for Gertrude B – the Department of Rural Development and Land reform that has been so generous previously. ENTER THE MEC WILLIAM BULWANE So Carte Blanche phoned the MEC of Agriculture and Rural Dev and asked him if he knew about the project and how it will be financed. (recorded conversation) No he said, but he would find out. He said he didn’t know Gertrude Bohloka (not true, he does, and we can prove that ) but he was very nice and promised to get back to us, so we didn’t push the fact he has already been caught out lying by CB. According to Mxolisi Dukwana our timing is good because Ace’s people are trying to distance themselves from him – “so he might help you’ says Dukwana. Just to put this money into perspective – Sun Valley farm managed to break even, pay salaries and all debt in 9 months with around R5 million and some borrowed tractors. All they wanted from their department was a R12 million rand loan and it never came. NOW LETS GO TO MEGA POULTRY IN VIRGINIA Here in the Matjhabeng municipality you will find the Virginia Mega poultry project. In 2014, two years after Gertrude began her farming venture, R30 million rand was spent on five broiler houses meant to house 40 000 chickens and meant to transform the lives of rural women. A year later another R9 million was spent and again R13 million in 2017 when the project was supposed to be complete. ( In China they build a hospital in ten days but anyway…) From the air this is what it looks like – and we have these pictures because poor old enthusiastic chicken man Charles Vauquelin hoped to get that business up and rolling too and flew over the area. But he didn’t succeed despite his proposals, and today the farms stand idle. (SEE BELOW) We also have a number of picture of Wildealskloof taken in 2012 when the farm was in good condition. Gertrude Bholoka will likely send Carte Blanche on a wild goose chase but now that we have spoken to the MEC it is going to be difficult for him to duck and dive. Still trying to find out a bit more on who built the Virginia Mega Project but I don’t think that will be too difficult. Both Charles V and Ollie Le Roux will go on camera. We can drone over the farms if access is denied but Ollie says he can get us on to Wilde Els Kloof. Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 11 December 2020 Script: THE GREAT FREE STATE CHICKEN FIASCO FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 4th OCTOBER 2020 Commentary One You may remember Ollie Le Roux as a provincial and Springbok front row forward, making his mark in the toughest position in a very tough sport. Up sound Ollie scores try Derek Link What you may not know is that he also made his mark in the demanding arena of poultry farming right here in the Free State Commentary Two Ollie met us on his farm just north of Bloemfontein Up sound Ollie and Derek Commentary Three But it’s not rugby, but his first farm Wildealskloof that I am here to talk about, because Le Roux has first- hand experience of how a land reform project can go horribly wrong. Music up sound By 2012 he had built the farm into a profitable business with 16 broiler houses and a contract with Supreme to take 500 000 chickens every week Ollie It was a strong contract and if you farmed well you made money Derek Link in 2012 Le Roux sold his farm to the state. The farm was then leased to a beneficiary -Getrude Bohloko for five years. The chickens were already bringing in a healthy revenue, all she had to do, was keep it going and reap the benefits Derek The bottom line is a beneficiary could make good money out of the farm? Ollie Very good. Commentary Four This valuation around the time of the sale, shows the state valued the farm at almost R42 million rand, with the assets ranging from average to good condition. Derek Just to refresh your memory I am going to ask our producer to show you these pictures of the farm at that stage Ollie That old chair you guys are going to get me all emotional now.. Commentary Five These photos were part of an official asset verification done in 2013 -and listed almost every item Le Roux had left for the new owner. Ollie The infrastructure you know it looks easy but jis, it takes a lot of stress and strain, but it’s a privilege to be able to create something like this Derek How did you feel about selling the farm Ollie? Ollie To leave it, and leave the people that you …it’s like leaving rugby. There is a lot of emotion in the land so I understand why land is such a powerful thing for people. Commentary Six The price agreed upon was R39.5 million voetstoets, and by 2013 Getrude Bohloko’s company was running the farm. Chickens up sound But just two years later Supreme cancelled the valuable contract. It seems Bohloko didn’t honour her side of the agreement and began costing them money. Then her company tried to go it alone Ollie They never understood how precious the contract is, and everybody thinks we can do it on our own, but trust me Derek you don’t understand 500 000 chickens with blood and feathers, you need big infrastructure and if the market goes against you, you are sitting with 500 000 frozen product. It’s a very tough game Derek Link Fast forward to 2017, and these pictures in our possession tell a sad story, of a farm stripped and broken, the 500 000 chickens gone, the broiler houses closed up, and a few dirty pigs lying in muck. Commentary seven Workers weren’t paid and apparently some may have vandalised the farm, but Bohloko refused to participate in our story, to give her side of events Derek Ollie we are going to show you pictures of the farm in recent years, I don’t want to upset you but this is what it looks like Ollie Ay ay ya the old fiat in sy moer…Oh donder! Yoh that was a massive infrastructure you know with this we could work 500 animals a day with three people. Yoh the generators are gone and that is a lot of money gone. And it’s being vandalized… Derek So to recap that farm now Ollie Ollie You can do it but it’s going to cost what it cost to buy it Derek So who has lost out really? Ollie Everybody has lost. Derek The state has lost Ollie And 38 people you can just imagine that’s 120 families and there was such a hope this would be a flagship project. Just to look at it is just so sad Commentary eight How Land reform beneficiaries are chosen has been described as an opaque process, and more than one recent official report has red flagged how elites are muscling in to get farms. Sources alleged, Getrude Bohloko was one of those elites. Up sound Steven Modise an official in the Free State Land reform office, was part of the process that helped Bohloko get Wilde Alskloof. Derek What criteria were used to select Getrude Bohloko as a beneficiary? Steven Actually she presented the offer of this farm to the department. Once you've identified your interest and your needs, you automatically become matched with a particular farm. And then once she was matched with a farm, obviously we acquired the farm as a department and then she then enjoys a lease Commentary nine At the time Modise was a director at Free State Land reform and recommended the funds be released for Wildealskloof. Our sources say it was Modise who wangled farms for elite beneficiaries Derek Steven we have independent sources telling us that you decide which politically connected people get the farms that are worth over R20 million? Steven Well it’s the first time I am hearing that I have never done anything for anybody, and for your information I am seated here today because I am the acting chief director acting for the last 3- 4 months – I am not involved in the allocation of farms, I am not involved… Derek Apparently you have been the go between Steven Well I didn’t know I was Commentary ten Bohloko’s lease expired in 2017 and her agreement with the state was to look after the assets or risk having the lease cancelled, that didn’t happen -instead it was decided last year to extend her lease for 30 years. Modise also told me the department visited the farm every quarter Derek But why didn't you step in when it was clear that the farm was failing and in fact being stripped Steven The farm was not failing, it was not stripped. In fact the stripping of the farm, If I were to tell you as far as I can recall when we bought the farm around 2012 was by the previous owner Mr. Leroux, who actually stripped the farm… so it was never stripped by any of our beneficiaries. Commentary eleven Le Roux says that’s a blatant lie and certainly the state’s own valuation and audit documents contradict Modise. The assets were considered in fair to good condition at the time of the sale. Derek But if you've been visiting on a quarterly basis have you not seen what's happening there? Just have a look at these pictures and you tell me that's not a farm going to wrack and ruin. Steven No, we know what is happening on the farm. These are the assets that were bought from Mr. Ollie Le Roux - They were bought in that state in a worse state Derek So you're saying those are the assets that she inherited in 2012? Steven No she didn't inherit the assets like this. But I want to come to that to actually explain to you. Derek Just to say that we've got pictures of when they were handed over. Steven Well you are saying they have been stripped? By whom? I don't know. LINK Two years after Wildealskloof was handed over, another chicken project about 150 kilometres north was under construction. The Virginia Mega poultry project- five broiler houses each with a capacity of 40 000 chickens Commentary twelve This poultry project, was built by E’tsho Civils, who said it would be complete by 2016. But six years since construction began and more than R52 million rand later, the project is at a standstill. E’tsho civils only director, is alleged in Pieter Louis Myburgh book, Gangster State to be close to ANC SG, Ace Magashule, who threatened to sue the author and hasn’t yet. Dr Roy Jankielson So it’s a huge financial basket with no eggs. Commentary thirteen THE DA’S Roy Jankielsohn has a PHD in Land reform modelling and has been on the Free state portfolio committee for Agriculture for 14 years. Roy In the Free State, agricultural projects are set up for the sole purpose of benefitting implementing agents and their cronies in government. I don’t think projects are set up in the FS to contribute to food security or assist beneficiaries on the ground Derek That is a strong statement Roy Roy It is a strong statement and I would stand by it because we have the necessary proof in the Free State Commentary fourteen Recently he has visited a number of farming projects and was shocked at the state of their decay. Here at Diyatalawa agricultural village, which cost R150 million rand – the dairy has been plundered, the apple trees are sticks, and just this gatehouse and fence alone, cost R600 000. Roy And I would challenge the MEC or any government official to prove otherwise- go and find us a project that is sustainable Commentary Fifteen MEC William Bulwane of the Department of Agriculture in the Free State disputes that, and has invited Carte Blanche to view their successful projects, which we will hopefully take up with them in the near future Derek I'm saying to you MEC see that the allegations are clear these projects are there to benefit the contractors who built the infrastructure, and the officials who hand out the contracts not the beneficiaries. In other words. Billions are being squandered- there is fraud, there is corruption, there is mismanagement? MEC Bulwane I like your word when you said allegations. It's a big word. Anybody squandering government money you know what must happen. And you can't just be sitting here folding our arms and be happy that government billions have been squandered Derek But you know they have? MEC Where? where? Derek What about the Estina Project? MEC Maybe you know where money has been squandered. I don't know? You must tell me so that when I leave from this seat I go there and take action. Derek Okay I'll give you two examples, you've got Wildealskloof you've got Virginia within about 150 kilometres of each other -and that's cost nearly a hundred million rand with nothing to show for it? MEC Now that you are talking figures I want the HOD to answer that question and then this billions you're talking about. I don't know where do you get them? Commentary sixteen Over the last five years R1.2 billion has been spent on farmer support in the Free State. It appears no one has done monitoring and evaluation to see if the funds were wisely spent to ensure beneficiaries become successful farmers, and even the auditor General can’t get an accurate picture because there are inadequate systems to record vital information. Derek MEC are you denying that a lot of money has been squandered? MEC No no, no… Derek In corruption and mismanagement in the Free STATE MEC We are not answering questions about corruption here, and I am saying this project we can account for, and I won’t agree with you that there is corruption Derek You will not agree that there has been any corruption in the Free State? MEC You have seen it yourself? Derek I have done programmes on it. What would you call Estina? The Virginia project, what would you call any of the projects that have lost millions, and have nothing to show for it MEC From where I am sitting, there is no money that has been squandered in Virginia, there is no money that has been squandered in that poultry project here Derek MEC you say there has been no squandering of money but neither project is operational?! MEC The Virginia project was operational, the water was getting inside those houses so they had to stop and build a storm water drainage Commentary seventeen So a new contractor was called in to fix the problematic storm water. The MEC had summonsed Dr Masiteng to answer specifics about Virginia, but most had already been answered by the MEC. Masiteng defended the R52 million price tag but did concede that the department needed to strengthen accountability Derek What is the plan for Virginia now? MEC They just need a strategic partner, once they have a strategic partner to share the expenses, and then they can move with speed. Commentary eighteen While it appears that nothing is moving with speed at Wildealskloof – behind the scenes there are new plans for the farm even though in eight years Bohloko only paid her R150 000 annual lease, once. Derek Link It may seem odd that having failed at farming, Getrude Bohloko now wants to build an abattoir on her farm Commentary nineteen And the speculation is that it’s unlikely the private sector would fund Bohloko’s abattoir Derek Some people say that the poultry abattoir is just a way to siphon off money? Ollie I believe they are 100% correct. Where are you going to find money for a poultry abattoir you will go to the IDC or the DTI and you are going to go to the bank. Trust me the banks aren’t going to look at you. The IDC they are too sharp so they not going to fund a project like that I know them too well. But where are you going to get it you are going to look for a grant and just siphon of money and it’s going to cost the taxpayer money. Rather start the farm again let’s do it with banks money but to take our tax money build an abattoir that is guaranteed to fail, I believe that is where we as SA must say enough is enough now Commentary twenty Bohloko was clear she didn’t want to speak to us, but I gave it another shot anyway Derek And you still propose going ahead with the poultry abattoir? Gertrude I have confirmed in writing with Miss Summers and the poultry abattoir and the EIA is handled by the department of environmental affairs …please refer to the feedback I have given to miss Summers Steven Modise If she is bringing investment into that asset, that is the kind of beneficiary we want Derek But who is going to pay for that abattoir? Steven Modise She is sourcing her own funds Derek She is not asking for state funding? Steven Modise No, no Derek Putting it simply shouldn’t another beneficiary be given a chance to run that farm? Steven Modise We are not convinced that she has failed so much, that that farm cannot operate. That farm needs production capital, that farm needs a contract, so obviously once those things are in place that farm will get back into operation Commentary twenty- one But Bohloko had all that back in 2013, a debt free, operational farm worth R40 million. A management team left by Le Roux to help her, plus a government mentorship programme and a ten year offtake agreement for the chickens. It may only be one example, but we are told there are many others, and if this is how the Free State is managing their land reform projects, perhaps it’s time for a radical rethink. THE END 16 05 PROMO ONE Two Free State Poultry projects – cost to taxpayer close to R100 million. Both are at a standstill. We go to the top to find out what went wrong. PROMO TWO Former Springbok Rugby player Ollie Le Roux speaks out about the profitable poultry farm he sold to the state that now lies in wrack and ruin. PROMO THREE The Virginia Mega poultry project was meant to uplift local women. But six years and R52 million rand later and the project is still not operational. We go in search of those responsible and find that even as the president promises to clamp down on corruption, out of the public eye, on the plains of the Free State, the politically connected are still going about their business. WildealsKloof or Two Geese, one rugby player and no chickens Eight years ago rugby player Ollie Le Roux sold his prime farm just outside Bloemfontein for R35 million rand to the Free State Department of Agriculture and Rural development. It was fully operational with 500 000 chickens, 300 pigs, 45 sheep and two cattle. There were 16 broiler houses, a cattle feedlot, 38 pigsties, 201 hectares of grazing ( CB has the official documents and photo’s taken of the audit at the time- even down to the desk and chairs.) The total registered value at the time was R38 million rand (land and immovable assets) and the lucky beneficiary was Gertrude Bohloko’s company Two Geese Trading. According to Ollie Le Roux the farm would have given Ms Bohloka a very comfortable income and enable her to easily pay of the R150 000 rand monthly lease fee to the department. But by 2016 Bohloka had run the farm into the ground and pleaded poverty. She took Liberty to court to try to access her pension fund but lost the case, and her 5 bedroom, 3 bathroom home in Fichardt Park was auctioned off by ABSA.
metadata.Further information: WHO IS GERTRUDE BOHLOKA? Three independent sources have told Carte Blanche she is extremely powerful, connected to Ace Magashule and casts fear into the hearts of lesser mortals. The man who arranged the farm for her in the department – Steven Modise would drop everything to attend to her when she phoned. THE FATE OF WILDEALSKLOOF Now in 2020 the farm is in dire need of love and care – items have been stolen and the once busy farm is a shadow of its former self and the only activity says Ollie Le Roux is Gertrude on her mower mowing the lawn, which is unusual he says. Le Roux has a second farm across the road and has watched his former farm which he built from scratch disintegrate. Sometimes he helps his former workers with food when Bohloka just doesn’t pay them. By 2017 the 5 year lease expired and despite the fact that Bohloka had not fulfilled the written provisions of the lease which is in Carte Blanche’s possession, her lease was renewed – apparently for another 30 years (confirmation required on duration) ENTER CHICKEN MAN CHARLES VAUQUELIN Charles Vauquelin is a straight shooting, turnaround chicken man. He can take any failed chicken venture and turn it into a profit and what he saw on Wildealskloof broke his heart. So he approached Gertrude B and every other influential person he could think of in Bloemfontein including the ANC, a business man and various others, to sub lease the farm from Bohloka for R150 000 per month, and use the existing infrastructure to farm chickens. He had a market, and all the plans in place. He also met with MEC William Bulwane and Gertrude Bohloka to try and broker a deal. But Gertrude refused to budge and by February this year Charles went to Rainbow in KZN to work there. He will go on camera and can fly us over the farm should we wish. Charles and Ollie Le Roux are not mates. But what is interesting about both their experiences is that they both tried separately to reinvigorate the farm and both hit a stumbling block that independently of each other, they believe is political. So eight years later the farm remains idle and the infrastructure either collapsing or stolen. BUT WAIT THERE IS MORE While Wildealskloof is a lovely farm by all accounts, it has a shortage of one critical thing, water. Carte Blanche has been told by a reliable source that in and around 2012, at least 5 boreholes were drilled and no water was found. Over the years an arrangement was made with the neighbouring farm to pipe additional water into the farm but it seems Bohloka has fallen out with the neighbour. ANOTHER DAY, ANOTHER PLAN So it would seem odd then to introduce the idea of building a chicken abattoir on the farm with insufficient water. Because if there is one thing an abattoir needs its water. But Two Geese trading – Bohloka’s company is pushing ahead and the EIA for the abattoir is already underway and has been confirmed by Carte Blanche in writing and with the man doing the EIA – Danie Krynauw. SO WHAT IS THE PROBLEM? The water is one thing: “where will all the blood and the feathers go? “asks Charles. It’s a crazy idea. There is also no need for another abattoir in the region, there are already too many, says our secret source, and when he heard about the idea his immediate response was this is yet another attempt to siphon off millions from the state. Try R80 million rand at least. And if Gertrude goes to a private bank for the money, it’s unlikely she will get a loan based on her not too stellar history in the chicken business; the fact that she doesn’t own the farm; and that there is no water on it. Which likely leaves only one avenue for Gertrude B – the Department of Rural Development and Land reform that has been so generous previously. ENTER THE MEC WILLIAM BULWANE So Carte Blanche phoned the MEC of Agriculture and Rural Dev and asked him if he knew about the project and how it will be financed. (recorded conversation) No he said, but he would find out. He said he didn’t know Gertrude Bohloka (not true, he does, and we can prove that ) but he was very nice and promised to get back to us, so we didn’t push the fact he has already been caught out lying by CB. According to Mxolisi Dukwana our timing is good because Ace’s people are trying to distance themselves from him – “so he might help you’ says Dukwana. Just to put this money into perspective – Sun Valley farm managed to break even, pay salaries and all debt in 9 months with around R5 million and some borrowed tractors. All they wanted from their department was a R12 million rand loan and it never came. NOW LETS GO TO MEGA POULTRY IN VIRGINIA Here in the Matjhabeng municipality you will find the Virginia Mega poultry project. In 2014, two years after Gertrude began her farming venture, R30 million rand was spent on five broiler houses meant to house 40 000 chickens and meant to transform the lives of rural women. A year later another R9 million was spent and again R13 million in 2017 when the project was supposed to be complete. ( In China they build a hospital in ten days but anyway…) From the air this is what it looks like – and we have these pictures because poor old enthusiastic chicken man Charles Vauquelin hoped to get that business up and rolling too and flew over the area. But he didn’t succeed despite his proposals, and today the farms stand idle. (SEE BELOW) We also have a number of picture of Wildealskloof taken in 2012 when the farm was in good condition. Gertrude Bholoka will likely send Carte Blanche on a wild goose chase but now that we have spoken to the MEC it is going to be difficult for him to duck and dive. Still trying to find out a bit more on who built the Virginia Mega Project but I don’t think that will be too difficult. Both Charles V and Ollie Le Roux will go on camera. We can drone over the farms if access is denied but Ollie says he can get us on to Wilde Els Kloof.
